title: Percentage of Confirmed COVID-19 Cases for Each Country in Relation to Total Arrivals from Those Countries
what_it_is: Percentage of Confirmed COVID-19 Cases for Each Country in Relation to Total Arrivals from Those Countries

sections.label: COVID-19 insurance for travellers
sections.summary: Imported case proportions were 0.04%, 0.01%, 1.6% and 3.7%; from 1 January 2021 Work Permit and S Pass holders need medical insurance, and from 1 February 2021 short-term visitors need travel insurance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The proportion of imported cases out of the arrivals from each of these countries and regions was 0.04%, 0.01%, 1.6% and 3.7% respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: From 1 January 2021 onwards, all Work Permit and S Pass holders are required to have medical insurance to pay for COVID-19 medical treatment and hospitalisation costs in Singapore, should the pass holder develop symptoms or test positive within the first 14 days of arrival into Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: From 1 February 2021 onwards, all short-term visitors applying to enter Singapore under the Air Travel Pass and Reciprocal Green Lanes have to purchase travel insurance for their COVID-19-related medical treatment and hospitalisation costs in Singapore.

sections.label: Review of insurance requirement
sections.summary: The Government will review extending the insurance requirement to other travellers, considering COVID-19 situations in their country of origin and insurance market product availability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Government will review whether to extend the insurance requirement to other travellers, taking into consideration the COVID-19 situations in their country of origin, as well as the availability of products in the insurance market.
